stages.title: Aggregate supply (AS)
stages.sub: How to read and draw the AS curve, and tell a movement along it from a shift of it.

steps.q: Across the whole economy, prices of most goods rise together, and total output is measured for the whole country rather than one firm. What are we now looking at: one firm's price, or the economy-wide picture?
steps.wrong: Still one firm's price and output
steps.hint: Think nationally, not about a single shop.
steps.pre: So we now track the whole economy's

steps.q: At a higher general price level, firms can sell their output for more. Are firms willing to produce and sell more output at that higher price level?
steps.hint: Would higher prices make production more or less profitable for firms overall?
steps.pre: The total output firms are willing and able to supply at each price level is

steps.q: If you plot the general price level on the vertical axis and real output on the horizontal axis, and higher prices mean firms supply more, which way should the line slope?
steps.hint: More output goes with higher price level, so as one rises, so does the other.

steps.q: The price level rises and firms respond by supplying more output, staying on the same AS line. Has the AS line moved, or have firms just moved to a different point on it?
steps.right: They moved to a different point on it
steps.wrong: The whole AS line has moved
steps.hint: Only the price level changed here, nothing about costs or conditions.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: Wages fall across the economy, so at every price level it is now cheaper for firms to produce, and they supply more output than before at each price level. Does one point move along the old line, or does the whole line move?
steps.wrong: It stays on the same line
steps.hint: This time the price level did not cause the change, costs did. So can the old line still describe firms' behaviour?

steps.q: Costs of raw materials for firms rise sharply. Should this be shown as a movement along the AS line, or as the AS line itself shifting?
steps.wrong: A movement along the AS line
steps.hint: Did the price level cause this change, or something else about firms' costs?
